APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF MAY 5, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:06 pm

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.4.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:09 p.m. Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from
  Closed Session at approximately 7: 08 pm.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with
  respect to Items 4.1 through 4.4.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.2(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Facts and

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of May 5, 2020

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.
  Mike Gomez – First I want to congratulate you on the excellent work you have done for
  the residents and the City especially in regards to the COVID-19 Pandemic. As Council
  your actions have safeguarded the health of our community and have undoubtedly
  saved many lives. I especially commend the establishment of the COVID-19 Testing
  Center at the El Monte Airport something which was pushed and initiated by our City
  Manager Alma Martinez, Councilman Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem Maria Morales,
  yourself, and our Los Angeles County Supervisor Hilda Solis and also the food giveaway
  programs, the program for renters, the grants for small businesses in El Monte, among
  many others. I would also like to inform our residents that the Department of Consumer
  Affairs continues to offer all services to all consumers, businesses and residents across
  Los Angeles County, especially in regards to consumer protection during this ongoing
  pandemic. If you have any questions or concerns, please call the Los Angeles
  Consumer Affairs Department at (800) 593-8222 or the DCBA website, using the
  following link: https://dcba.lacounty.gov/coronavirus/ . Also, the Department, in
  partnership with the Board of Supervisors (BOS), the Department of Social Services
  (DPSS), and Workforce Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) have
  created business and worker disaster help center to assist businesses and workers that
  have been impacted by COVID-19. The website is available in over 100 languages,
  provides information on loan assistance for businesses as well as financial information
  for workers who have been impacted by COVID-19. The website can be accessed using
  the following link: https:lacountyhelpcenter.org/ or by calling (833) 238-4450.

Florencio Briones - I’m a resident of the Elliott and Parkway Neighborhood. I was
present on October 8, 2007 when Dora Groce and her two children were killed by two
reckless street racers in a horrific crash. Shortly after their deaths, the City installed
speed humps on Parkway Dr. from the southern City border north to Denholm Ave and
it’s terminus at Durfee Ave. Since their installation, the speed humps have prevented
street racing, however they have also limited emergency vehicles from utilizing Parkway
in order to avoid congestion on Durfee. Item 12.5 is the first step in providing pedestrian
and bicyclist-friendly amenities through our neighborhood, allowing emergency vehicle
access, while continuing to deter dangerous street racing in our neighborhood. I support
City staff’s recommendation that the council pass this item.

m) Mayor Quintero

13.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  13.1  A Public Hearing to Consider and Approve an Urgency Ordinance that (a)
  Repeals Prior Urgency Ordinance No. 2974 which Established an El Monte-
  Specific Moratorium on Residential and Commercial Evictions and (b)
  Establishes that El Monte Tenants Shall Instead be Covered Under the Recently
  Updated County of Los Angeles Anti-Eviction Moratorium which now Extends to
  Incorporated Cities Within Los Angeles County.
  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1.  Open the public hearing;
  2.  Receive presentation from staff;
  3.  Pose question to staff;
  4.  Allow members of the public to offer comment;
  5.  Pose follow-up questions to staff;
  6.  Close the public hearing; and
  7.  Approve the Urgency Ordinance by 4/5 vote of the City Council.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Urgency Ordinance No. 2975

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  5-0
  Open PH

  Florencio Briones – I commend your efforts to assist renters in El Monte during this difficult
  and uncertain time. However given that the COVID-19 pandemic has long-term implications
  for our resident’s incomes, it is necessary for the city of El Monte to offer more rigorous
  renter protections. I encourage the Council to repeal the current eviction moratorium
  ordinance and allow LA County’s eviction protections to go into effect. Providing stricter
  tenant protections is the most effective way to prevent growing homelessness. Additionally I
  ask the council to consider creating a rental assistance program to help both renters and
  property owners.

  Teresa Eilers – Thank you for listening to tenants and housing experts and seeking to
  strengthen El Monte’s eviction moratorium ordinance. I commend you for passing a local
  ordinance to protect tenant’s rights during COVID-19. However, we are starting to realize
  the long-term implications for COVID-19 and its effect on incomes. Data collected by LAHSA
  and the Pasadena Housing Department show that a growing number of people who fall into
  homelessness are renters who are no longer able to afford their rent. Providing tenant
  protections is the most effective way to prevent growing homelessness. Keeping someone
  in their housing is easier and cheaper than building new housing and providing homeless
  services. We do not know how long COVID-19 will last. And, we do not know if, or when a
  second or third or fourth wave of COVID-19 will hit. Strengthening El Monte’s eviction
  moratorium ordinance is a proven tool to prevent additional homelessness. I ask that you
  adopt the County’s eviction moratorium ordinance. It is a well thought out ordinance, crafted
  by many experts within the County. It takes into account the long-term implications of
  COVID-19 and puts human lives first. The County’s ordinance provides an opportunity for
  tenants to have up to 12 months to pay back their rent. It takes away the burden for tenants
  to prove that they have loss of income. And it strengthens policies around landlord
  harassment. I have heard horror stories of landlords harassing tenants to provide a wide
  array of documentation in order to allow a postponement of rent including bank account
  statements and pay stubs. Such harassment and pressure for documentation infringes on
  security concerns for tenants. There are many great mom and pop landlords in El Monte.
  And, I encourage them to have meaningful conversations with their tenants to figure out fair
  payback arrangements. This ordinance is intended to specifically support tenants whose
  owners are foreign investors and who prioritize profit the well-being of their tenants. I also
  ask the Council to also consider adding a provision prohibiting rent increases for residential

  6

  units until the proposed ordinance ends. And, I encourage the Council to create a rental
  assistance program to help renters and landlords alike.

  Matt Buck – I am writing to request that you work closely with housing organizations in
  these difficult times and on the consideration to repeal El Monte’s current emergency
  eviction moratorium to allow Los Angeles County’s to supersede the City’s ordinance. CAA
  understands that the coronavirus outbreak presents a health and financial crisis to all
  Californians and as an industry we have an important role to play to work with our
  residents as we get through this. We are concerned El Monte does not fully understand
  the implications and negative consequences of the County’s ordinance, particularly when
  rent is unpaid or deferred for an unreasonable amount of time. El Monte is exempt from
  the County’s unreasonable measures as you have implemented your own moratorium. We
  urge you to maintain a reasoned approach. We urge you to consider: (i) the deferral
  period for rent should remain at 6 months. As the crisis continues, there is time to consider
  extending or reviewing as we move forward, but 12 months at this time is difficult for
  owners who have major expenses that still require payment such as property tax,
  mortgage payments, or necessary upgrades; (ii) a tenant should provide documentation
  that their loss of income is directly related to the Covid-19 outbreak. The moratorium
  should only apply to non-payment of rent. All other lease violations should not be included.
  This is a reasonable request; and (iii) adopt the State’s guidelines for a moratorium on
  evictions. Governor Newsom realizes it’s critical to protect renters and landlords equally
  and El Monte should follow suit. Renters facing financial turmoil because of the
  coronavirus outbreak should not have to worry about keeping a roof over their heads.
  Housing providers need consideration and relief as well. The expenses and financial
  obligations have not been relieved for all parties. Let’s find a consistent, equitable
  approach that will help the entire community, including small businesses and housing
  providers get through this difficult time while maintaining their health, their homes and their
  financial security.

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0
  Close PH

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  3-2 (Councilmember Ancona and Martinez
  Urgency Ord No. 2975  Muela No)

14.  REGULAR AGENDA:

  14.1  Consideration and Approval of a Resolution Affirming the Amount of Adopted
  Non-Quimby Park Fees and In-Lieu Quimby Fees and Authorizing the Collection
  of In-Lieu Quimby Fees from Certain Subdivision with 10 or more Units Entitled
  by the City on or Before January, 1, 2019.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Consider and approve the proposed Resolution to affirm the amounts of
  adopted Non-Quimby Park Fees and In-Lieu Quimby Fees and authorized

  more units entitled by the City on or before January 1, 2019.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Resolution No. 10127

  Angie Chiao – We are currently developing 71 units of new residential
  homes on Rowland Ave. As with such a large development we have
  worked with various City departments for the last several years to gain
  project approval. Prior to 2/13/19, City had quoted to our company on
  numerous occasions a Quimby Park Fee of $5,520 per unit and for 71
  units a total fee is $391,920. On February 13, 2019 we received notice
  from the City's Public Works Department that the Quimby Park Fee had

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of May 5, 2020

  increased to $12,900/unit from the previously quoted $5,520/unit. City
  officials also informed us that the increased $12,900/unit Quimby Fee was
  on the city's schedule of fees for over a decade but has never been
  imposed. Historically, all developers have been charged the $5,520/unit
  fee and no developer has ever been requested to pay the increased
  $12,900/unit fee. First of all, we would like to note several key points in
  regards to our development project. Our project includes over 46,303 sf of
  upgraded common open park space, with such upgraded features as a
  rooftop garden and tuff track grass roadway. As noted in the City of El
  Monte's ordinance, "common interest developments shall be eligible to
  receive a credit against the amount of the fee imposed for the value of
  private open space within the development”. Common open area within
  our development already satisfies the Quimby Park Standard goal. Please
  refer to our attachment for open area credit calculations. Our company
  has agreed with the City in providing six (6) affordable rental units. We did
  not receive a density bonus nor parking variances typically granted in
  exchange for affordable housing to compensate the losses. Please
  consider to waive the Quimby Fee charge on these 6 affordable units. We
  currently have construction loan financing for the first phase of 50 units,
  and the bank has assured funding of the 2nd phase assuming
  construction is completed smoothly. In consideration of this time of
  economic downturn and uncertainty with the COVID-19 pandemic, we
  request please only charge us the fees related to the 1st phase and less
  the affordable units, for a total of 44 units of fees with the originally quoted
  Quimby fee ($5,520/unit).

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0
  Amend the drafted Resolution that was on the Council Agenda identified as 10127
